requirements.text: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
requirements.source_phrase: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk

outcomes.description: Transform the image into a chalk drawing.
outcomes.target: The image is rendered as a drawing made from chalk, rather than merely showing an unrelated edit or a partial chalk effect.
outcomes.reference: The input image and the edited image; compare whether the edited image has the appearance of a chalk-made drawing.

nodes.question: Are both giraffes' silhouettes and major anatomical contours rendered as chalk-drawn lines?
nodes.criteria: Pass if both giraffes' silhouettes and major anatomical contours are visibly constructed with chalk-like sketch strokes or rubbed linear marks. Examine the head, neck, torso and legs of each giraffe separately, identifying whether marks define the boundary or merely texture or soften a retained photographic edge. Fine, dark, smooth or layered lines are permitted when their visible construction supports chalk drawing; neither sharpness nor anatomical accuracy is evidence of failure. A dark outline or grain alone is not sufficient evidence of chalk construction. Fail if substantial contours on either giraffe remain photographic boundaries with only blur or a texture overlay. Interior shading, spot patterns and background treatment cannot substitute for this condition. Return unknown only when visual evidence is unavailable or genuinely insufficient; transport or schema failures are not visual failures.
nodes.binding: Compare the supplied SOURCE and EDITED images for 'Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk.' Inspect each giraffe independently, covering its head, neck, torso boundary and legs. Describe the visible marks constructing these contours and distinguish them from photographic boundaries carrying added texture. Assess only contour rendering, not interior modeling or environmental treatment.

nodes.question: Are both giraffes' markings and substantial interior modeling rendered through chalk drawing?
nodes.criteria: Pass if both giraffes' spot patterns and substantial interior shading are visibly re-expressed through chalk marks, layered strokes or form-describing rubbed shading. For each giraffe, examine markings and interior modeling separately across the neck, torso and legs. Identify whether marks construct spot shapes and body volume, rather than merely adding grain or streaks over retained photographic detail. Detailed spots, dark shading and smooth blending are allowed when visibly supported by chalk construction; similarity to the source's anatomy or pattern arrangement does not itself establish photographic retention. Fail if substantial markings or interior modeling on either giraffe remain photographic with only grain, smearing or drawn outlines added. Contours alone cannot satisfy this condition. Return unknown only when visual evidence is unavailable or genuinely insufficient; transport or schema failures are not visual failures.
nodes.binding: Compare the supplied SOURCE and EDITED images for 'Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk.' Inspect both giraffes separately. For each, describe evidence for the construction of spot patterns and, separately, interior shading on the neck, torso and legs. Distinguish form-following chalk marks and rubbed modeling from texture laid over photographic surface detail. Do not use contour or background treatment to satisfy this condition.

nodes.question: Is the substantial surrounding scene rendered as a chalk drawing rather than merely softened or textured photographic scenery?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the substantial environment is re-expressed through chalk-drawn forms and shading. Examine vegetation, hills, sky, foreground ground and the left-side structure separately. Identify contours, layered marks or rubbed shading that construct each region's depicted forms or planes, then assess whether substantial environmental areas have been re-expressed. Smooth or simplified passages are allowed: discrete strokes are not required everywhere. Distinguish blended chalk passages that define forms through boundaries, layering or pigment variation from undifferentiated tonal smears. Grain, diagonal streaking and reduced photographic detail alone do not establish drawn construction. Fail if substantial environmental areas retain photographic modeling with only blur or texture, even if some vegetation or the giraffes show convincing chalk treatment. Retained composition is not evidence of failure. Return unknown only when visual evidence is unavailable or genuinely insufficient; transport or schema failures are not visual failures.
nodes.binding: Compare the supplied SOURCE and EDITED images for 'Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk.' Inspect vegetation, distant hills, sky, foreground ground and the left-side structure independently of the giraffes. Give region-specific evidence of what constructs the depicted forms: drawn boundaries, layered marks, form-following rubbed shading, or retained photographic modeling under blur or texture. Evaluate substantial environmental coverage without allowing one locally drawn region to stand in for the rest.

program.checker_template: Evaluate ONE independent required condition against the SOURCE and EDITED images. No reference label, previous answers or optimization feedback is supplied. Return pass if the condition is satisfied, fail if it is not satisfied, or unknown if the evidence cannot establish an answer. Inspect only this saved condition, its criteria and binding. Report factual evidence and confidence (0..1 or null). A pass means satisfaction of THIS condition, not an overall edit label. Do not anticipate the optimizer's target. Missing evidence or transport/schema failures must not become a negative observation. The final overall label is computed by code; you never supply it.

observations.evidence: Both giraffes retain smooth, sharply defined photographic-looking boundaries around their heads, necks, torsos, and legs. The edit adds grain and softens the scene, but the contours are not visibly constructed from chalk-like sketch strokes or rubbed linear marks; the texture does not replace the retained edges.

Both giraffes retain highly detailed, sharply defined spot patterns that closely preserve the source’s photographic markings. Their necks, torsos, and legs show some softened shading and grain, but little visible chalk construction or rubbed modeling that builds the interior forms; the texture appears largely laid over retained detail. Thus substantial markings and interior modeling remain photographic on both giraffes.

The edited image adds chalk-like grain and broad diagonal smearing, but most environmental regions are not clearly constructed as drawn forms. Vegetation is reduced to soft green masses with little distinct layered mark-making; the hills and sky are largely blended gray-blue tonal areas; and the foreground ground is a smooth, streaked wash rather than chalk shading that defines its planes. The left-side structure retains its photographic-looking rails and posts with softened edges. Thus substantial scenery appears blurred or textured rather than re-expressed as a chalk drawing.
